Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Jonas Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Rachel Kim (PulseCare Head of ML), Samir Patel (PulseCare Platform), Olivia Chen (PulseCare Security), Marcus Green (PulseCare CTO)
summary: Discovery focussed on migration from OpenAI-hosted models to Redwood Dedicated (and potential Private) for PulseCare Health. Main concerns: model compatibility (vLLM/TGI inference parity), latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (KMS/SOC2/SSO), and evaluation parity. Agreed to run a benchmark/pilot and exchange security docs.
topics: Security / compliance (KMS, SOC 2, SSO, audit logs)
Pilot / benchmarking plan and success criteria
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i've got Jonas from our SE team as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marcus (PulseCare): good thanks, we've got about 50 minutes, hoping to figure out if dedicated makes sense for us.
[00:12] Maya: perfect, quick agenda, we'll run through your current infra, goals, constraints, then dig into compatibility questions vllm/tgi and security, then next steps. sound good?
[00:20] Rachel (PulseCare): sounds great, thanks. to start, we use OpenAI for prod now, plus some self-hosted vllm for batch tasks. main issue is token cost and occasional rate limits during peaks.
[00:32] Samir: and we hit variable latency some of our interactive workflows need sub 300ms p99 and that's hard at scale with the hosted provider.
[00:40] Jonas (Redwood SE): helpful. when you say you run vllm, are you running TGI in parallel anywhere or primarily vLLM?
[00:47] Rachel: primarily vLLM, we experimented with TGI for some flavor-of-ly smaller models, but production is vllm on our k8s clusters.
[00:55] Jonas: ok cool. quick note: Redwood Dedicated supports the same model formats we serve on hosted, and our runtime is compatible with the common vllm/TGI checkpoints, but there are nuance  quantization, kv cache handling, and any operator mismatches can cause tiny eval diffs.
[01:10] Rachel: that was my main worry  eval parity. we ran a suite against OpenAI and our in-house vllm and saw some variance, want to avoid regressions.
[01:18] Maya: totally. typical approach is side-by-side evals with your prompt set and a small pilot; we can pin model versions and provide a regression report. we'll also surface kernel selection/quantization choices.
[01:28] Marcus: and how about throughput  can dedicated keep up with our bursts? we have unpredictable spikes tied to patient intake windows.
[01:36] Jonas: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and configurable autoscaling with burst policies. practical throughput depends on model and batch size; we usually recommend a live benchmark with your rate profile. we can simulate your 1M token/day burst pattern.
[01:48] Olivia (Security): can i ask about encryption and key management? we need KMS integration and customer-managed keys.
[01:54] Maya: yes, Private supports BYOK with KMS/HSM, Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS for secrets and you get audit logs. we'll send the security whitepaper.
[02:04] Olivia: also need SOC 2 and SSO/SAML support for RBAC.
[02:08] Maya: we have SOC 2 and SAML SSO; RBAC and audit trails are part of the console. i'll include the doc links.
[02:14] Samir: back to compatibility  if we migrate model checkpoints from vLLM, is there a required conversion step? last time we had to recompile some ops.
[02:22] Jonas: sometimes yes  especially custom ops or bespoke tokenizer behavior. for mainstream Llama-family checkpoints it's straightforward, but for TGI artifacts we sometimes need small conversion patches. we can collaborate on a checklist.
[02:34] Rachel: what's the expected latency improvement vs hosted? our biggest pain is p99.
[02:38] Jonas: Dedicated with colocated GPUs usually improves p99 by 20-40% for same model/config, and you get consistent tail latencies due to reserved capacity. caching and micro-batching in our runtime also help. exact numbers vary  that's why we propose a benchmarking run.
[02:52] Marcus: cost  will this actually save us versus OpenAI?
[02:55] Maya: commonly yes at scale. we provide cost models  dedicated is commit-based pricing that reduces per-token unit cost, and we have Optimize recommendations (quantization/batching) to hit targets. we'll send a model-specific cost projection.
[03:08] Rachel: for the eval parity i want specifics: if we run 10k prompts and see a 1-2% delta in scoring, is that acceptable? what thresholds do you see in similar migrations?
[03:18] Jonas: usually small diffs happen at the tokenization or quantization boundaries; diffs under ~3% on metrics are typical and often explainable. if you need strict parity we can run tuning  kernel selection, disable some quantization passes, or use fp16 paths.
[03:34] Olivia: auditing  do you provide request-level logs and redaction? our PHI policy requires redaction and retention controls.
[03:42] Maya: yes, retention policies and PII/PHI redaction options are available; for Private deployments you can keep all logs in your VPC. for Dedicated we support redaction and configurable retention.
[03:54] Samir: timeline  if we want to pilot, how long to get a dedicated env up?
[03:59] Jonas: typical pilot onboarding is 2-4 weeks depending on model complexity and infra approvals. Private on-prem can take longer.
[04:06] Marcus: approvals will need legal + security signoff; Olivia will lead.
[04:10] Olivia: yes i'll need the compliance pack.
[04:13] Maya: noted  we'll send SOC2, pen test summary, and an HLD for Dedicated. link (shared): https://redwood.ai/security/pulsecare-pack
[04:22] Rachel: what about model fallbacks  if a newer model isn't supported, can we automatically route to an older variant?
[04:28] Jonas: yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallbacks to compatible variants or hosted endpoints. that helps availability during upgrades.
[04:36] Marcus: for the pilot, can we run our 10k eval suite and the 1M token production replay?
[04:41] Maya: absolutely, that aligns with our recommended benchmark. we'll coordinate runbook and metrics (latency, cost, top-line quality differences).
[04:50] Rachel: sample prompts and datasets, i'll upload to the shared drive after this call.
[04:54] Maya: great. quick caveat  transcription/ops: some model-specific plugins might need small changes; we can estimate effort after we see the checkpoints.
[05:02] Olivia: legal questions  contract SLAs and data residency, we need EU data residency for some data.
[05:09] Maya: Dedicated allows region pinning and Private is an option for strict residency. we'll note that in the pilot scope.
[05:16] Samir: curious about observability  how granular are the token-level cost breakouts?
[05:20] Jonas: console exposes per-route and per-model token count, cost breakdown, traces and error events; we can also forward metrics to your prometheus/observability stack.
[05:29] Marcus: ok let's recap.
[05:31] Maya: recap: Redwood to send pricing/pilot contract, SOC2/security pack, benchmark runbook. PulseCare to share eval prompts and 10k test set and confirm pilot window week of 12/14. SE to prepare benchmark config.
[05:44] Rachel: yeah that works.
[05:46] Maya: any other questions?
[05:47] Olivia: none from security for now.
[05:48] Marcus: all good. thanks everyone.
[05:50] Maya: thanks all, i'll send notes and next steps after the call. shared artifacts: pilot playbook (https://redwood.ai/pilot-playbook), Dedicated pricing (attached in email).
[05:58] End of recording

Notes on transcript quality: a few terms may be transcribed incorrectly (vllm sometimes appears as 'v-l m' etc), proper nouns like PulseCare or Redwood console occasionally miscapitalized.
